findings.v1Observation: Separate capability, input, and output arrays can match a tuple the provider never declared.
findings.control: Each provider declares unique capability/input/output route tuples with minimum input-artifact counts.

findings.v1Observation: Several scalar validators coerce non-string values before checking them.
findings.control: v2 requires exact scalar types, strict semantic versions, canonical UTC timestamps, safe integers, and lowercase digests.

findings.v1Observation: Provider and reference ordering uses localeCompare.
findings.control: v2 uses explicit code-unit lexical comparison and deterministic-json-core.

findings.v1Observation: A catalog cannot represent two versions of one provider id and a preference cannot bind descriptor bytes.
findings.control: Multiple versions remain visible; exact id, version, and descriptor digest selection is required when ambiguous.

findings.v1Observation: Observations have no expiry, explicit evaluation time, record digest, or observer trust intersection.
findings.control: v2 adds canonical times, maximum age, expiry, self-digest, exact observation selection, and explicit trusted observer references.
findings.openSeam: A copied or fabricated trusted observer reference cannot be authenticated by this pure planner; external signature or host-attestation verification remains required.

findings.v1Observation: A satisfying host observation may carry permissions beyond provider needs.
findings.control: v2 refuses missing or overbroad host permission, network, mutability, and source-use envelopes.
findings.openSeam: No executor exists here and no confinement behavior was tested.

findings.v1Observation: The planner carries no bounded-resource model.
findings.control: Provider needs, request ceilings, exact host envelopes, and a resource-enforcement verification reference are mandatory.
findings.openSeam: References are not dereferenced and no runtime resource measurement or enforcement occurred.

findings.v1Observation: The planner has no portable boundary preflight.
findings.control: A path-minimizing boundary reference rejects drive, UNC, ADS, traversal, device, trailing-dot/space, normalization, case-fold, nested, and source/output/evidence overlaps.
findings.openSeam: The pure validator performs no filesystem, symlink, junction, or destination-existence observation.

findings.v1Observation: Free evidence-ceiling text is copied into the route plan and no explicit content-retention truth fields exist.
findings.control: v2 route output carries opaque references, artifact sizes/digests, and an evidence-policy digest; it states that content and machine paths were not retained.
findings.openSeam: No future executor or evidence writer is implemented or authorized.

findings.v1Observation: Verification primarily compares a rebuild and does not expose strict standalone plan normalization.
findings.control: Closed recursive schemas, strict runtime normalizers, self-digests, cross-field checks, and deterministic rebuild verification reject malformed output.

findings.v1Observation: Provider evolution and request inputs lack explicit parent and artifact byte references.
findings.control: Provider parents bind exact canonical descriptor digests and input artifacts bind declared byte digests and lengths.
findings.openSeam: The planner does not read artifact bytes or replace Module Evolution Ledger ancestry authority.

findings.v1Observation: The planner cannot distinguish research-only inspection from direct byte reuse.
findings.control: Transform/copy providers receive REUSE_RIGHTS_HOLD unless an exact declared authority reference is supplied.
findings.openSeam: A reference is not a legal sufficiency finding; Mike's reuse-rights decision remains deferred.
